title: Happy Head vs FutureClinic: compounded hair formulas or a standard prescription
summary: Happy Head vs FutureClinic compares hair loss costs, compounded refills, and a $40 FutureClinic visit. A doctor reads your case and answers by message.
body_markdown:
[Happy Head](https://www.happyhead.com/llms.txt) treats[hair loss](https://futureclinic.com/blog/hair-loss-treatment-online-without-a-subscription) online with custom-compounded bottles and capsules billed on a default 25-day refill cycle ($49 for the first order, then $63.20 per refill or $79 once as of October 2026).[FutureClinic](https://futureclinic.com/) connects you one to one with an expert physician for $40 (or a chosen doctor's price, typically $20 to $100) with no subscription required and nothing attached, sending any prescription your doctor decides is right for you to the pharmacy you choose.


On FutureClinic, no form is approved in bulk. A specific doctor reads your whole case and answers with a Human Signature, a live video or voice note recorded for you. Whenever you check back in, you write to the same doctor in that ongoing thread, building trust as you test hair treatments and review progress: comparing crown and hairline photos over months, adjusting a dose if side effects show up, or swapping a topical formula that irritates your scalp. The dermatologist managing your hair loss can also care for other skin concerns in their specialty, like acne or eczema, and every FutureClinic doctor you see works from your[one medical record](https://futureclinic.com/blog/one-online-doctor-for-everything-vs-condition-apps) .


## How Happy Head and FutureClinic compare side by side


What to compare Happy Head FutureClinic


Who treats you FAQ: "board-certified Happy Head dermatologist licensed in your state"; terms: "medical doctors, physicians, and other health professionals" Licensed physicians only holding an MD, DO or MBBS degree (no NPs or PAs)


What you pay (as of October 2026) $49 first order, then $63.20 per 25-day refill, or $79 once $40 for the best-fit doctor, or a chosen doctor's price (typically $20 to $100)


Subscription required? 25-day default subscription, or $79 once No subscription required; optional membership typically $25 to $100/month


Where medicine comes from Compounded monthly by Curexa or Chemistry Rx; no local pharmacy The pharmacy you choose, including retail and mail-order delivery


What else the doctor treats Hair loss, dandruff, scalp, beard, brow, and one hair-and-ED formula Other problems in their specialty; every FutureClinic doctor you see works from your one medical record


How you reach them Messaging on happyhead.com; no MCP server or AI app By message on futureclinic.com or from your AI app


What you get back Messages and compounded bottles; reply time and video not stated Plan and Human Signature; replies typically within a few hours, almost always the same day or the next


## Who treats you?


Founded by board-certified dermatologists ([llms.txt](https://www.happyhead.com/llms.txt) ), Happy Head covers male and female hair loss, dandruff, scalp health, beard and brow formulas, a laser helmet, a DNA test kit, and one dutasteride-tadalafil formula for hair loss and erectile dysfunction ([sitemap](https://www.happyhead.com/sitemap.xml) ). Its[FAQ](https://www.happyhead.com/faq) says "you will be assigned a board-certified Happy Head dermatologist licensed in your state," while its[Terms & Conditions](https://www.happyhead.com/legal/terms-of-use) (updated May 15, 2026) state that Kulanite Specialized Services Inc. and M&D Integrations Inc. employ or contract with "medical doctors, physicians, and other health professionals." Choosing or keeping a clinician is not stated.


FutureClinic connects you with over 300 doctors across the United States. Those physicians span more than 60 specialties, including both generalists and specialists, and every clinician is a state-licensed, background-checked doctor with an MD, DO or MBBS degree, never a nurse practitioner or physician assistant. Because the clinic does not sell drugs, the physician caring for you earns nothing extra for any prescription or test. Their only incentive is to help you: there is no product line pushing an upsell on medications or labs, no recurring plan needed to keep a prescription, and, if your doctor decides it's right for you, they can send whichever brand or generic medicine fits you to any pharmacy, controlled medicines excepted. The dermatologist treating your hair can also treat acne, rosacea, or eczema in their specialty, including oral isotretinoin (Accutane) with iPLEDGE by message from dermatologists who offer it.


First, an AI assistant trained by your doctor asks about your history, medicines, and photos. At FutureClinic, we believe AI is a tool for doctors and the human physician must stay in charge, since only a trained expert can catch when an algorithm makes a mistake. Rather than directing care, our AI works behind the scenes like a chief resident organizing your intake notes, and it never gives medical advice by itself. Once you approve the intake summary, your physician reviews the entire chat, makes every clinical decision, and sends your plan with a Human Signature, replying typically within a few hours and almost always the same day or the next.


## What does a year of hair loss treatment actually cost?


As of October 2026, Happy Head prices its[Topical Solution (finasteride plus minoxidil)](https://www.happyhead.com/products/topical-solution-finasteride-minoxidil) and oral[SuperCapsule (finasteride, minoxidil, and vitamin D3)](https://www.happyhead.com/products/supercapsule-finasteride-minoxidil-vitamin-d3) at $49 for the first order (with a free telehealth visit), then $63.20 per refill, or $79 once. Its[FAQ](https://www.happyhead.com/faq) states, "Billing and shipping intervals are set at 25 days by default," and you can pause, skip, or cancel through customer service. Twelve orders ($49 plus 11 refills) cost **$744.20** , while 14 orders on the 25-day schedule cost **$870.60** over 350 days. Because Happy Head does not use local pharmacies, you stay subscribed or pay $79 per bottle to keep using it.


On FutureClinic, there is no[subscription](https://futureclinic.com/blog/telehealth-subscriptions-vs-paying-a-doctor-per-visit-yearly-cost) required. You pay $40 to match with the best-fit doctor, or pick a specific doctor at their listed price, which is typically $20 to $100. If your doctor decides it's right for you, your prescription goes to the pharmacy you choose, including retail chains and mail-order pharmacies that deliver to your door, with a discount coupon for the best cash price. You can use insurance at the pharmacy, and FutureClinic helps get a prior authorization when insurance needs one.


For a stable medicine, your doctor can prescribe several months at once when they judge it safe. As of October 2026,[GoodRx](https://www.goodrx.com/finasteride) lists 30 tablets of finasteride 1 mg at $14.93 in its dosage table (average retail $45.44), with standard coupon prices of $10.20 at Sam's Club, $16.99 at Costco, and $29.45 at CVS. Two $40 visits ($80) for six-month prescriptions plus 12 fills at those coupon prices totals **$202.40 to $433.40 for the year** for finasteride alone (Happy Head's price also includes minoxidil), or less with insurance. For ongoing access, most physicians also offer an optional membership, typically $25 to $100 a month, giving you unlimited care with that doctor (cancel any time), with your visit fee credited if you join afterward.
